heading: EXT. MARATHON AID STATION - MILE 22 - 3 A.M.

units.text: EXT. MARATHON AID STATION - MILE 22 - 3 A.M.
A folding table under a sodium streetlight.
Paper cups in rows.
A cooler of orange slices.
The course winds into the dark.
OTTILIE MARSH, 60s, in a reflective vest, tops up cups from a jug.
PAVEL DVORAK, 30s, a volunteer, sits on a camp chair and stares at the road.
YOSHIRO TANABE, 40s, a medic, arranges bandages in a tackle box.
Ottilie finishes the row.
She wipes her hands.
She glances at the road, then at Pavel.
He does not look at her.
She slides a cup across the table.
He takes it.
He holds it without drinking.
Anyone coming?
units.name: YOSHIRO

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: They'll be a while. The leaders passed an hour ago.
units.name: PAVEL

units.text: I'd run it again.
units.name: YOSHIRO

units.text: You would not.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: I would.
units.name: YOSHIRO

units.text: She smiles.
He does not.
Pavel gets up and stands at the edge of the light.
He puts the cup down on the table without a word.
After a moment she follows his gaze.
It was last year, wasn't it.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: I'm fine.
units.name: PAVEL

units.text: She walks to the table, takes up the jug, and carries it to him.
She holds out a full cup, and he accepts it with both hands.
Headlights.
units.name: YOSHIRO

units.text: They all turn.
A lone runner appears at the edge of the dark, slow and swaying.
Pavel steps forward with the cup held out in front of him like an offering.
